questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All drums are balloons.

No rings are balloons.

All rings are keys.

Conclusions:

(I) No drums are rings.

(II) Some keys are not drums.
questions.solution:
Given Statements:

All drums are balloons.

No rings are balloons.

All rings are keys.

The Venn diagram representation for the given statements is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31644e5940eab7e69b8a62fa7f3dc1a7fb20e165eff494191ba5d276161d2a03.png] 

Conclusions:

**(I) No drums are rings. → **True (If no rings are balloons, and all drums are a part of balloons, then no drums can be rings.)

**II) Some keys are not drums. **→ True ("All rings are keys" and "No rings are balloons". Since "All drums are balloons", it means rings (which are also keys) cannot be drums. Therefore, the portion of keys that are rings cannot be drums. This directly implies that some keys (specifically, the rings) are not drums.)

So, Both conclusion (I) and conclusion (II) follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
